findings.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards turn duplicate `[Key]` values into a silent member drop. A `[MessagePackObject]` type with two members both `[Key(0)]` (or both `[Key("a")]`) used to throw on `Dictionary.Add`, which surfaced as an AD0001/CS8785 warning. Now the second member is skipped, and no visible code in these hunks reports a MsgPack diagnostic for the collision. Unless a uniqueness check exists elsewhere, the generated formatter omits a member with no warning, which loses data silently.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.DuplicateKeyDiagnosticReceipts.DuplicateIntKeys_ReportsMsgPackError and DuplicateStringKeys_ReportsMsgPackError. Each compiles a type with duplicate keys, runs all DiagnosticAnalyzers from the generator assembly plus the generator, and asserts at least one Error-severity MsgPack diagnostic. They fail on head if the duplicate is silently dropped.

findings.claim: The same silent-drop guard is duplicated in the second member loop (fields), so duplicate keys on fields are also dropped without a diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Same receipt class; variant with duplicate [Key(0)] on two public fields: DuplicateIntKeysOnFields_ReportsMsgPackError.
